extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: A question answering data set consisting of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine, paired with Wikipedia pages and annotated with long and short answers.
extraction.creator: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Queries issued to the Google search engine are filtered, run through the search engine, and paired with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results to be sent to human annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine and Wikipedia pages from the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries of 8 words or more are filtered using simple heuristics based on syntactic patterns to discard non-questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators determine if a question is good or bad, select the earliest HTML bounding box containing enough information for a long answer (or mark no answer), and then select an entity or set of entities for a short answer (or yes/no/no short answer).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Post-hoc evaluation of correctness by experts and analysis of 25-way annotations to study human variability, disagreement, and ambiguity in acceptable answers.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 for training data, 5 for development and test data, and 25 for a subset of 302 examples.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential biases due to the choice of Wikipedia as the sole source of factual information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of open-domain question answering systems.

name.evidence: This paper introduces Natural Questions (NQ), a new data set for QA research

description.evidence: We present the Natural Questions corpus, a question answering data set. Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. An annotator is presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results,and annotates a long answer (typically a paragraph) and a short answer (one or more entities)

creator.evidence: Tom Kwiatkowski... Slav Petrov Google Research

publisher.evidence: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, vol. 7, pp. 453–466, 2019.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We run questions through the Google search engine and keep those where there is a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results. The (question, Wikipedia page) pairs are the input to the human annotation task

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine... An annotator is presented with a (question, Wikipedia page) pair.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine... keep those where there is a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Simple heuristics are used to filter questions from the query stream... All the questions in NQ are queries of 8 words or more... From these queries, we sample a subset that either: 1. start with 'who', 'when', or 'where'...

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The guidelines and tooling divide the annotation task into three conceptual stages... Question Identification: Contributors determine whether the given question is good or bad... Long Answer Identification: For good questions only, annotators select the earliest HTML bounding box... Short Answer Identification: For examples with long answers, annotators select the entity or set of entities...

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: Annotation is performed using a custom annotation interface, by a pool of around 50 annotators

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We also describe analysis of 25-way annotations on 302 examples, giving insights into human variability on the annotation task... One clear finding in NQ is that for naturally occurring questions there is often genuine ambiguity in whether or not an answer is acceptable.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: The public release consists of 307,373 training examples with single annotations; 7,830 examples with 5-way annotations for development data; and a further 7,842 examples with 5-way annotated sequestered as test data... analysis of 25-way annotations on 302 examples

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Part of speech tags and entities are identified using Google’s Cloud NLP API

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We focus on Wikipedia as it is a very important source of factual information... however, like any data set there may be biases in this choice.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The public release consists of 307,373 training examples... 7,830 examples... for development data; and a further 7,842 examples... sequestered as test data... We propose NQ as a new benchmark for research in QA.
